title: Ciletuh Geopark Run 2027 Review: A Ministry-Backed Race in a UNESCO Geopark
seo_title: Ciletuh Geopark Run 2027 Review | Sukabumi, Indonesia
meta_description: Ciletuh Geopark Run 2027 review: January 17 at Palangpang Beach -- Indonesia's Tourism Ministry backing a race in a UNESCO Global Geopark since 2018.
dek: Set for 17 January 2027 at Palangpang Beach, this race runs through Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu Geopark -- recognised by UNESCO as part of the Global Geoparks Network since April 2018, backed directly by Indonesia's Ministry of Tourism.
verdict: The Ciletuh Geopark Run carries the direct backing of Indonesia's Ministry of Tourism as part of the broader Geopark Run Series -- the same series covered at the Ijen and Minang legs elsewhere in this research batch, now extending to Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu, a 128,000-hectare UNESCO Global Geopark recognised nationally in 2015 and internationally in 2018. Three distances (5K/10K/21.1K) put it in line with the series' other legs. Ministry-level backing gives this race genuine institutional weight beyond typical commercial sponsorship.

sections.heading: A Third Geopark Run Series Leg
paragraphs: The Ciletuh Geopark Run offers three distances -- 21.1K, 10K and 5K -- at Pantai Palangpang, Sukabumi, West Java. [1] It's the third leg of the Geopark Run Series covered in this research batch, following the Ijen Geopark Run's volcanic-highland debut and the Minang Geopark Run's canyon-and-clock-tower course -- extending the series to a third distinct Indonesian geological landscape.

sections.heading: A UNESCO-Recognised Geopark
paragraphs: Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu Geopark spans 128,000 hectares across 8 districts and 74 villages of Sukabumi Regency, recognised as a national geopark by UNESCO in 2015 before joining the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network in April 2018. [2] Attractions within the park include Puncak Darma (its highest point), waterfalls like Curug Sodong and Curug Awang, Palangpang and Palabuhanratu beaches, and Lalay Cave -- a genuinely varied geological and coastal landscape for the race to run through.

sections.heading: Direct Ministry Backing
paragraphs: Unlike the Ijen and Minang legs, which are organised under the general Geopark Run Series brand, this Ciletuh event is explicitly backed by Indonesia's Ministry of Tourism (Kementerian Pariwisata). [1] That direct government-ministry involvement gives the race genuine institutional weight, similar in spirit to Malaysia's tourism-board-backed Selangor and Penang Bridge marathons covered elsewhere in this research.

sections.heading: Registration Status: Coming Soon
paragraphs: Registration is listed as 'coming soon' -- more specific than the simple 'not yet announced' status seen at many other races in this research batch, suggesting an imminent opening. [1]

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want to run through a UNESCO-recognised geopark with direct national tourism-ministry backing, the Ciletuh Geopark Run on 17 January 2027 is a strong pick within the growing Geopark Run Series. Watch for registration to open soon, per the current status listing.

faqs.question: Is this related to the Ijen and Minang Geopark Runs?
faqs.answer: Yes -- Ciletuh is the third leg of the same Geopark Run Series covered at Ijen (volcanic highlands) and Minang (canyon country) elsewhere in this research, now extending to a third distinct Indonesian geological landscape. [1]

faqs.question: What makes Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu a UNESCO-recognised site?
faqs.answer: It's a 128,000-hectare geopark spanning 8 districts and 74 villages of Sukabumi Regency, recognised nationally by Indonesia in 2015 and joining UNESCO's Global Geoparks Network in April 2018, featuring waterfalls, beaches and sea caves. [2]

faqs.question: Is registration open?
faqs.answer: Listed as 'coming soon' -- more specific than many other races in this research still marked simply 'not yet announced,' suggesting an imminent opening for the 17 January 2027 race date. [1]
